title: Everything to Play For
description: Talking about yourself and your family with the four word families of the lesson: FAMILY (grandparents, grandfather, mum, dad, cousin, relatives), FOOD (vegetables, carrots, recipe, fruit, grapes, cooking), LEISURE (play, games, reading, instrument, music, cards) and ANIMALS (pet, dog, cat, bird, elephant, mouse), every word learnt inside a sentence and sorted into its field; describing a person with the character adjectives sociable, kind, bright, dull, childish and naughty, and never leaving an adjective without the fact that proves it (Yes, she is kind: she cooks for her grandparents), then comparing yourself to that person (we are alike, I am like her, I am different from her); reading a paragraph and choosing its title from a closed list of eight (Cooking, Learning and playing music, Leisure activities, My favourite music, Pets, What I think of some jobs, The food I like, My grandparents), separating the near-twin titles and agreeing on one broader title for the whole text; writing a similar paragraph about yourself; and the lexical traps of a French speaker (parents versus relatives, sensible versus sensitive, sympathetic, actually versus at present, play the violin but play football, fruit, food and music uncountable)
